Devin: heads up — saw a pretty bad perf regression in KV cache hit-rate after a driver rolling deploy this morning, likely related to keying + kernel selection mismatch. profiling attached below.

Maya: ugh, how bad are we talking?

Devin: ~45% token throughput drop for small-chat baseline (gptx-7b-quant zstd), median latency up 2.1x. KV lookups went from ~92% hits -> ~27% hits after restart. heap + cache miss counters spike at the same time.

Sam: did the model version change or just the driver binary?

Devin: driver binary + kernel selection table updated (arch heuristics tuned). model binary (weights) unchanged. But kernel fingerprint we use in keys now includes the kernel_version string, which changed. Missing persistence semantics meant we treated all cached entries as incompatible.

Priya: hmm. that suggests our keying is too strict. we need a more discriminative policy: stable model identity vs ephemeral runtime attributes.

Devin: exactly. proposal: split key into two layers — stable key (persisted) and runtime fingerprint (in-memory index). stable key = model_id + model_hash + quant_profile + seq_len_bucket. runtime fingerprint = driver_kernel_hash + arch_flags + kernel_impl_id. When runtime fingerprint mismatches, we should try to replay/validate entries rather than GC immediately.

Maya: can we validate lazily? e.g., keep persisted entries on disk but mark as "stale-potential". On first access, run a quick compatibility check (lightweight verify of kv metadata + checksum). If it passes, promote to current runtime; if not, evict that entry. That avoids mass invalidation during rolling restarts.

Devin: yes. lazy validation is what I had in mind. For safety we add a TTL (configurable) for persisted entries so old caches don't linger forever. Also add a conservatively small in-memory fast-path: if seq_len_bucket differs by >1 bucket, avoid reusing.

Sam: what's the compatibility check cost? worried about adding CPU to the critical path.

Devin: cheap — check stored quant_profile id, embedding dims, and a 64-bit checksum of the KV blob. if checksum mismatch or dims mismatch -> evict. In practice it adds ~200ns median extra on cache hit path (we measured). That's acceptable compared to a full miss.

Priya: what about kernel selection heuristics? if kernel impl changed to a new fast-path optimized for long sequences, some short-seq entries might still be valid but suboptimal. should we prefer runtime fingerprint -> choose lower-latency kernel but allow fallback to older kernel if data found?

Devin: plan: keep kernel selection separate from cache keying. Use a kernel compatibility matrix: for each persisted entry, store the kernel ABI tag we used to produce KV. On resume, if ABI differs but is known compatible (per matrix), we accept. If ABI differs and unknown, perform a quick op to validate correctness (apply 1 step). We'll treat incompatible as miss.

Maya: love the matrix idea. where do we store it? onboarded kernels + compatibility flags in runtime config pushed via orchestration. ops-bot can notify services when matrix updates.

ops-bot: infra:kernel-matrix updated -> drivers (all regions) will receive new matrix version 2026-03-17T08:00Z.

Sam: persistence storage — disk per-node or shared?

Devin: prefer shared object store for long-lived persisted KV (S3/GCS) with local LRU cache on node for hot entries. keys include stable key prefix to namespace by model/hash. local cache invalidation on node restart still required but longer-term persistence survives driver redeploys.

Priya: what about security/PII concerns storing cached prefixes? need to ensure no sensitive prompt material persists.

Devin: agreed — we only persist model-internal KV blobs (attention caches) which are deterministic given model weights + prompts. but we should strip any raw prompt text. plus encryption-at-rest + per-tenant keying enforced. add a compliance flag to disable persistence for regulated tenants.

Maya: can you drop a short RFC with: key format, TTL defaults, lazy-validate flow, matrix definitions, and perf numbers you measured? then we can triage for next sprint.

Devin: will do. rough key format (proto):
```
stable_key = f"m:{model_id}|h:{model_hash}|q:{quant_profile}|s:{seq_bucket}"
runtime_meta = f"k:{kernel_impl_id}|v:{kernel_version}|a:{arch_flags}"
storage_key = stable_key  # persisted namespace (runtime_meta stored as metadata)
```

Devin: perf numbers from today's run (microbench baseline):
- baseline (pre-rolling): 14.8k tokens/s, KV hit 92%
- post-rolling (current master): 8.2k tokens/s, KV hit 27%
- with lazy-validate POC on local node: 13.6k tokens/s, validation overhead ~200ns/hit

Sam: that's promising. any regression risk from validation code itself? i/o spikes?

Devin: IO only on cache miss or on validation failure. we batch validation ops and prefetch hot entries during startup to avoid thundering herd. wrote a small benchmark: prefetching 500 hot keys serially took ~120ms; we can parallelize.

Priya: ok — priority: (1) RFC + tests, (2) small PoC behind flag on staging, (3) run load test with rolling driver deploys, measure hit-rate and token throughput.

Maya: I'll own the staging rollout. Sam — can you review kernel compatibility matrix section?

Sam: on it.

Devin: thanks y'all. will post RFC link here when ready. :rocket:
